items.title: 14.4.5 Coplanar Vectors and Condition for Coplanarity of Three Vectors

blocks.text: Vectors are coplanar if they lie in the same plane or can be combined in the same plane.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: "Can be combined in the same plane" means: a vector may be moved parallel to itself without changing it, so vectors are coplanar if, after moving them to start from one point, they all lie in one plane.
Consider the three coplanar vectors \(\underline{u}\), \(\underline{v}\) and \(\underline{w}\) in a plane as shown in the figure.

blocks.alt: A grey plane with three vectors u, v and w drawn in it from one point. The vector v x w rises from that point perpendicular to the plane, with right-angle marks at its foot. As in the print, each letter carries a small arrow over it.
blocks.caption: Figure: coplanar vectors u, v, w; v × w is perpendicular to the plane (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text: The cross product \(\underline{v}\times \underline{w}\) gives a vector that is perpendicular to both the vectors \(\underline{v}\) and \(\underline{w}\). As \(\underline{u}\), \(\underline{v}\) and \(\underline{w}\) are coplanar, so \(\underline{v}\times \underline{w}\) is also perpendicular to \(\underline{u}\).

Thus, the dot product of \(\underline{u}\) and \(\underline{v}\times \underline{w}\) is zero, i.e.,
\[\underline{u}\cdot(\underline{v}\times \underline{w}) = 0\]
\(\because\) If vectors \(\underline{a}\) and \(\underline{b}\) are perpndicular then \(\underline{a}\cdot \underline{b} = 0\).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints "perpndicular". The correct spelling is "perpendicular".
Thus, we conclude that if the three vectors \(\underline{u}\), \(\underline{v}\) and \(\underline{w}\) are coplanar then their scalar triple product is zero.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Why is \(\underline{v}\times \underline{w}\) perpendicular to \(\underline{u}\)? \(\underline{v}\times \underline{w}\) is perpendicular to the whole plane of \(\underline{v}\) and \(\underline{w}\) (like a flagpole standing on the floor), and \(\underline{u}\) lies in that plane (like a line drawn on the floor). In the language of 14.4.2: a box whose three edges lie in one plane is flat, so its volume is zero.

items: If \(\underline{u}\), \(\underline{v}\) and \(\underline{w}\) are coplanar, then the volume of the parallelepiped so formed is zero, that is \((\underline{u}\times \underline{v})\cdot \underline{w} = 0\), and hence the vectors \(\underline{u}\), \(\underline{v}\), \(\underline{w}\) are coplanar \(\Leftrightarrow (\underline{u}\times \underline{v})\cdot \underline{w} = 0\).

If any two vectors of scalar triple product are equal, then its value is zero, i.e., \([\underline{u}\ \underline{u}\ \underline{w}] = [\underline{u}\ \underline{v}\ \underline{v}] = [\underline{u}\ \underline{w}\ \underline{w}] = 0\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Property 1 works both ways (\(\Leftrightarrow\)): coplanar vectors give \(0\), and a zero triple product means the vectors are coplanar. So to test coplanarity, compute \([\underline{u}\ \underline{v}\ \underline{w}]\) and see whether it is \(0\).
For four points \(A, B, C, D\): they are coplanar exactly when \([\underline{AB}\ \underline{AC}\ \underline{AD}] = 0\) (Example 27).
Property 2: if two of the vectors are equal, two rows of the determinant are equal and the determinant is \(0\); geometrically, two equal vectors together with a third always lie in one plane.

blocks.title: Example 27
blocks.problem: Prove that four points \(A(-3, 5, -4)\), \(B(-1, 1, 1)\), \(C(-1, 2, 2)\) and \(D(-3, 4, -5)\) are coplanar.
steps:
Given: \(A(-3, 5, -4)\), \(B(-1, 1, 1)\), \(C(-1, 2, 2)\), \(D(-3, 4, -5)\).
To prove: the four points lie in one plane.
Method: the points are coplanar exactly when the three edges \(\underline{AB}\), \(\underline{AC}\), \(\underline{AD}\) from \(A\) are coplanar, that is when the parallelepiped on them has volume \([\underline{AB}\ \underline{AC}\ \underline{AD}] = 0\) (Property 1).

Step 1: Edge \(\underline{AB}\)
\[\underline{AB} = \underline{OB} - \underline{OA}\]
\[= (-1+3)\underline{i} + (1-5)\underline{j} + (1+4)\underline{k}\]
\[= 2\underline{i} - 4\underline{j} + 5\underline{k}\]
Why: end point minus starting point. Subtracting \(-3\) means adding \(3\), which is why \(+3\) appears.

Step 3: Edge \(\underline{AD}\)
\[\underline{AD} = \underline{OD} - \underline{OA}\]
\[= (-3+3)\underline{i} + (4-5)\underline{j} + (-5+4)\underline{k}\]
\[= 0\underline{i} - \underline{j} - \underline{k}\]
Why: same rule; the \(\underline{i}\)-component is \(0\).

Step 4: Set up the scalar triple product
\[[\underline{AB}\ \underline{AC}\ \underline{AD}] = \begin{vmatrix} 2 & -4 & 5 \\ 2 & -3 & 6 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: the rows are the components of the three edges.

Step 6: Conclusion
The volume of the parallelepiped formed by \(\underline{AB}\), \(\underline{AC}\), \(\underline{AD}\) is zero, so these vectors are coplanar. They all pass through \(A\), so \(A\), \(B\), \(C\), \(D\) lie in one plane.
Why: a box of zero volume is flat: all its edges lie in one plane.
blocks.answer: \([\underline{AB}\ \underline{AC}\ \underline{AD}] = 0\), so the points \(A\), \(B\), \(C\) and \(D\) are coplanar.

blocks.title: Example 28
blocks.problem: Find the value of \(\alpha\), so that \(\alpha\underline{i} + \underline{j}\), \(\underline{i} + \underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\) and \(2\underline{i} + \underline{j} - 2\underline{k}\) are coplanar.
steps:
Given: \(\underline{u} = \alpha\underline{i} + \underline{j} + 0\underline{k}\), \(\underline{v} = \underline{i} + \underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\), \(\underline{w} = 2\underline{i} + \underline{j} - 2\underline{k}\).
To find: \(\alpha\) for which the three vectors are coplanar.
Method: coplanar \(\Leftrightarrow [\underline{u}\ \underline{v}\ \underline{w}] = 0\). Write the triple product in terms of \(\alpha\), set it equal to zero and solve.

Step 1: Set up the determinant
\[[\underline{u}\ \underline{v}\ \underline{w}] = \begin{vmatrix} \alpha & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & -2 \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: \(\underline{u}\) has no \(\underline{k}\) term, so its third component is \(0\).

Step 2: Expand along the first row
\[= \alpha(-2 - 3) - 1(-2 - 6) + 0(1 - 2)\]
\[= -5\alpha + 8\]
Why: first term \(\alpha\big[(1)(-2) - (3)(1)\big] = -5\alpha\); second \(-1\big[(1)(-2) - (3)(2)\big] = -1(-8) = 8\); third has the factor \(0\).

Step 3: Apply the coplanarity condition
\[-5\alpha + 8 = 0\]
\[\alpha = \dfrac{8}{5}\]
Why: the vectors are coplanar exactly when the scalar triple product is zero.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
1. Coplanar vectors lie (or can be moved parallel to themselves to lie) in one plane.
2. \(\underline{u}, \underline{v}, \underline{w}\) coplanar \(\Leftrightarrow [\underline{u}\ \underline{v}\ \underline{w}] = 0\).
3. Four points \(A, B, C, D\) are coplanar \(\Leftrightarrow [\underline{AB}\ \underline{AC}\ \underline{AD}] = 0\).
4. A triple product with two equal vectors is \(0\).
5. For an unknown such as \(\alpha\): set the determinant equal to \(0\) and solve.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text:
1. Using the points' coordinates in the determinant instead of the edge vectors \(\underline{AB}, \underline{AC}, \underline{AD}\).
2. Taking the edges from different points, e.g. \(\underline{AB}, \underline{BC}, \underline{CD}\) mixed with others; all three must start at the same point.
3. Sign slips with negative coordinates: \(-1 - (-3) = -1 + 3 = 2\).
